Let $s_n = a x^n + b y^n$. Each $s_n$ satisfies a linear recurrence whose coefficients come from $x$ and $y$ themselves. Since $x$ and $y$ are roots of $t^2 - (x+y)t + xy = 0$, we have

$$s_{n+2} = p\,s_{n+1} + q\,s_n, \quad \text{where } p = x+y,\ q = -xy.$$

Using $s_2 = 7$, $s_3 = 16$, $s_4 = 42$ with $s_1 = 3$:

$$16 = 7p + 3q, \qquad 42 = 16p + 7q.$$

From the first equation, $q = \dfrac{16 - 7p}{3}$. Substituting into the second:

$$126 = 48p + 7(16 - 7p) = 112 + p \implies p = -14.$$

Then $q = \dfrac{16 + 98}{3} = 38$.

Check: $s_3 = -14(7) + 38(3) = 16$ ✓ and $s_4 = -14(16) + 38(7) = 42$ ✓.

Therefore

$$s_5 = p\,s_4 + q\,s_3 = -14(42) + 38(16) = -588 + 608 = 20.$$

ANSWER: 20
